graphEvents.label: Did the three workflows drift where they duplicate steps?
complete.yaml is a second copy of plan and implement

label: speckit-complete.yaml is a second implementation of plan and implement: its checkpoint list runs steps 1-14 plus four auxiliary steps, repeating plan steps 1-7 and implement steps 8-12, so every gate and confidence block exists in two copies.

confidence_framework.scoring_weights names three different models under one key: plan scores four planning factors, implement four implementation factors, complete seven web/API factors, so a confidence percentage is not comparable across commands.
circuit_breaker.states contradicts itself across the three files at the same failures 3 threshold: plan halts the workflow, implement skips the affected step, complete substitutes a fallback agent.

The pre-change discipline has three names and three lengths: plan lists 5 items under pre_change_validation, complete lists 9 including checklist_verified_L2_plus, implement renames the key to pre_implementation_validation with 5 different items.

Refutation: the documentation-level tables have not drifted; plan, implement and complete carry identical required_files per level and differ only in cosmetic loc_guidance strings, so the drift is behavioural rather than structural.

DEVIATION markers appear in 14 non-archived specs files against 4060 plan packets and debug-delegation.md exists once in z_archive, but the required deviations_from_plan section of implementation-summary.md is populated in 212 of 3945 summaries, so the marker is the emptier of two channels.

recommend-level.sh is invoked only inside the with-phases pre-workflow in plan and complete; implement never runs it, cites it only in level_selection.note, and skips its Level-2 acceptance step for Level 1, so the level that decides the gate is inherited.

Plan requires research/research.md as an output and never validates it, implement declares it optional, and 298 of 4060 non-archived plan packets carry one, so the workflow declares an output that most runs do not produce.
